program_name: Bachelor in Design and Art - Major in Art (Italian: Corso di laurea in Design e Arti, Curriculum in Arte; German: Bachelor in Design und Künste, Studienzweig Kunst)
teaching_language: Trilingual (Italian / German / English). The brochure 'At a glance' box states 'Courses will be taught in: Italian, German and English (trilingual)'. There is NO all-English semester. Based on the published 2026/27 course offering, the theory/lecture block of the first year is largely English — Project Warm-up ART 12 CP EN, Descriptive Geometry ART 6 CP EN, Artistic Production 6 CP EN, Artistic Practices 6 CP EN, History of Contemporary Art 1 6 CP EN, Interaction and Communication Design 6 CP EN, Sociology of Social Change 8 CP EN, Cultural Anthropology 8 CP EN, History of Design 6 CP EN, four 2 CP seminars EN, Foreign Language - English: Academic Skills 3 CP EN. But the Art major carries MORE hard-locked non-English coursework than the sibling Major in Design. Compulsory German-only courses in the Art study plan: Artistic Drawing 2D 8 CP, Drawing and Storytelling 6 CP, History of Contemporary Art 2 5 CP = 19 CP that cannot be taken in English. In addition, the compulsory choice group {Video and Post-Production 6 CP DE, Photography 6 CP DE, History and Criticism of Audiovisual Media 6 CP IT} contains NO English option at all, adding a further 6 CP — so at least 25 CP of compulsory credit is non-English. Other German-only courses in the offering: Typography and Graphics 6 CP DE, Design Theory 5 CP DE. The four 19-CP STUDIOS (76 CP, ~42% of the 180 ECTS and the pedagogical core) run as parallel atelier groups with mixed language tags in 2026/27: Studio A1 SPACE = IT/DE (no English group), Studio B2 INTERACT = DE/IT (no English group), Studio C1 IMAGE = DE/IT/EN, Studio C2 IMAGE = IT/EN, Studio D2 EXHIBIT = IT/EN/DE. [uncertain] — the per-language ECTS weighting is reconstructed from the 2026/27 course-offering listing (which shows only what is offered that year and assigns multiple language tags to studio groups reflecting parallel groups rather than one delivery language), not from an official language-split statement; language tags can differ from year to year.
campus: Bozen-Bolzano main campus, Faculty of Design and Art, Universitätsplatz 1 / piazza Università 1, 39100 Bozen-Bolzano, Italy. Teaching is studio-and-workshop based in the faculty building, with four dedicated studios: one devoted to SPACE (sculpture and installations), one to the VISUAL ARTS / IMAGE (photography, videos and film), one to INTERACT (performative arts / new media) and one to EXHIBIT (visual culture / curatorship). Work groups are small and supervised by three lecturers. Students must complete compulsory safety training (Work Safety - Machinery Hazard - Chemical Risk) before attending the technical workshop courses. This is NOT the NOI Techpark campus (Engineering), nor Brixen-Bressanone, Bruneck-Brunico, Trento or Innsbruck.
degree_class: L-4 (Disegno industriale / Industrial Design). 180 ECTS, 3 years. Note the national dual-enrolment rule cited in the admission document uses this class as its own example: simultaneous enrolment in 2 programmes is allowed only if they do not belong to the same class, 'e.g., L-4/L-4' and the two programmes differ for at least 2/3 of course contents. The Major in Art and the Major in Design are two curricula of the SAME L-4 degree 'Design e Arti / Design und Künste', so a candidate cannot enrol in both simultaneously.
offered_in_2026_27: Yes — actively offered, and as of the verification date (2026-08-29) it is one of the very few unibz programmes STILL OPEN for 2026/27 applications. The programme page states 'Courses will definetely be starting'. Unlike the sibling Major in Design (both quotas filled exactly, no further session), the Major in Art UNDERFILLED both regular sessions — 7 admitted in Early Bird against 18 places and 10 admitted in the Late session against 10 places, i.e. 17 admitted against 28 EU places, with no waiting lists in either session — and the Faculty therefore opened an ADDITIONAL APPLICATION SESSION running 18/08 - 04/09/2026 (EU citizens and citizens given parity of treatment only), which is open at the time of verification with six days remaining. Its interview is 16/09/2026 and its ranking list is due by 18/09/2026 (not yet published).
is_new_programme: No — an established programme of the Faculty of Design and Art. The faculty's online Showcase and Projects Archive covers student work 'since 2018' across the two Majors in Design, the Major in Art and the Master in Eco-Social Design. The structure was revised for the 2025 cohort: 'From the 2025 cohort onwards, all students are required to attend the "Warm-Up" introductory workshop courses', and the Study Guide publishes separate study plans for the 2025-onwards and 2022-onwards cohorts, with students enrolled before 2022/23 told to contact the Faculty Secretariat. [uncertain] — unibz does not publish a first-intake year for this programme or for the Art major specifically; 'not new' is inferred from the 2018-onwards archive, the multiple cohort study plans and the absence of any 'new programme' badge, not from an explicit statement.
majors_tracks_study_plans: The degree 'Design and Art' (L-4) is split into TWO SEPARATE MAJORS with separate quotas, separate ranking-list sections and partly separate procedures: Major in Art (this record) and Major in Design. Quota contrast for 2026/27 — Art: 18 EU Early Bird + 10 EU Late + 2 non-EU = 28 EU + 2 non-EU; Design: 34 EU Early Bird + 24 EU Late + 2 non-EU = 58 EU + 2 non-EU. The Art major is roughly half the size of the Design major, and it is the ONLY one of the two that opened an Additional Application Session in 2026/27 (18/08-04/09/2026, interview 16/09/2026). A candidate may apply for both majors but must then upload TWO different videos, one per major, and must reach at least 8/20 in the corresponding field of the practical creative work for each major applied to (8/20 in the Art field for the Major in Art, 8/20 in the Design field for the Major in Design). Within the Major in Art there are no separate admission tracks. The study plan is built around FOUR STUDIOS of 19 CP each (76 CP total), chosen by the student: Studio A 'Space' (Spaces and their Production 8 CP + Material Sciences and their Use in an Artistic Space Contest 6 CP + Sociology of Space 5 CP); Studio B 'Interact' (Interaction/Performance 8 + Experience Design 6 + Media Culture 5); Studio C 'Image' (Photography-Video 8 + Visual Communication 6 + Media Theory 5); Studio D 'Exhibit' (Exhibition as artistic Practice 8 + Exhibit Design 6 + Curatorial studies: Theory and practices 5). Selection rules: 'students have to choose 4 studios. Starting from the 2nd semester, students can attend only one project per semester. The Studio A and the Studio D can each be undertaken only once. The Studio B and the Studio C may be undertaken twice.' — so students can repeat one studio experience twice and customise their own path. The rest of the plan: 12 CP Project Warm-Up ART (6 CP Praxis + 6 CP Theory), 8 CP Artistic Drawing 2D, 6 CP Artistic Practices, 6 CP History of Contemporary Art 1, 5 CP History of Contemporary Art 2, 6 CP Drawing and Storytelling, 6 CP Artistic Productions, 3 CP Foreign Language - Linguistic Skills, 6 CP Descriptive Geometry ART; four compulsory choice groups — 1 of {Interaction and Communication Design 6, Typography and Graphics 6}, 1 of {Cultural Anthropology 8, Sociology of Social Change 8, Innovation Managing and Start-up 8}, 1 of {Foreign Language DES-ART 1 Italiano 3, Foreign Language DES-ART 2 Deutsch 3}, 1 of {Video and Post-Production 6, Photography 6, History and Criticism of Audiovisual Media 6}; 2 CP Seminar (pass/fail, compulsory attendance); 12 CP Free Choice Courses; 9 CP Degree Project. Workshop courses carry zero credits but attendance is mandatory: the 'Warm-Up' introductory workshops in semester 1 are compulsory to access the specialised workshops, and from semester 2 onwards at least two specialised workshops must be chosen and attended.
english_only_accessibility: effectively-closed. The language rule is eliminatory, not a tie-breaker: the admission document states the requirements apply 'otherwise you will be excluded from the admission procedure', and entry demands B2 in the 1st language AND B2 in the 2nd language. A candidate who can certify only English satisfies at most one language and is removed before scoring. Empirical proof from the 2026/27 Early Bird ranking list: the decree contains a non-EU section ONLY for the Curriculum in Design (5 applicants, all excluded for failing the language requirements) and NO non-EU section at all for the Curriculum in Arte — i.e. zero non-EU applicants living abroad even appeared on the Art list, and both reserved non-EU places went unused. On the EU side, 8 Early Bird and 6 Late applicants to the Art major were excluded for 'non risultano in possesso dei requisiti di ammissione' (not possessing the admission requirements), which for this faculty is overwhelmingly the language gate. Three important qualifications: (a) the second language does NOT have to be German — English B2 + Italian B2, English B2 + German B2 or Italian B2 + German B2 all satisfy the rule, so the programme is genuinely open to any bilingual candidate; (b) exclusion is recoverable between sessions — applicant 152730, excluded in Early Bird for lacking the requirements, returned to top the Late ranking list with 92/100, and applicant 152483, who scored 4/100 in Early Bird for not submitting the creative work, was admitted in the Late session with 63/100; (c) the ADDITIONAL SESSION (18/08-04/09/2026) publishes NO unibz Language Centre exam dates, so a candidate applying now must ALREADY hold a recognised certificate or qualify through their schooling — the exam route that existed in the Early Bird and Late windows is not available. Additional load once inside: graduation requires C1/C1/B2 across all three languages, and the Art major has notably more hard-locked non-English coursework than the Design major — at least 25 CP of compulsory credit (Artistic Drawing 2D 8 CP DE, Drawing and Storytelling 6 CP DE, History of Contemporary Art 2 5 CP DE, plus a 6 CP choice group whose three options are all DE or IT). Furthermore, in the 2026/27 studio offering, Studio A 'Space' ran as IT/DE only and Studio B 'Interact' as DE/IT only, while only Studio C 'Image' and Studio D 'Exhibit' had English groups; since students must complete FOUR studio instances and Studio C is the only one repeatable with an English group alongside a single Studio D, an English-reliant student cannot assemble four studio instances from English groups alone in that year's offering. [uncertain] — this last inference rests on the 2026/27 language tags, which reflect that year's parallel groups and may change.
admission_type: Restricted access (numero programmato) with a three-stage aptitude selection and a published merit ranking list. The instruments are: (1) a self-produced VIDEO (max 2 minutes) uploaded to the application portal — a prerequisite, not merely a scored item; (2) a PRACTICAL CREATIVE WORK carried out at home on a topic issued by e-mail about one week before the interview; (3) an ONLINE INTERVIEW of about 10-15 minutes before a commission composed of lecturers of the faculty. There is NO written entrance exam, no TOLC, no CENT-S, no SAT and no conventional portfolio submission. A prior language-eligibility gate (B2 in two of the three teaching languages) removes applicants before scoring. Separate ranking lists are drawn up for (a) EU citizens and citizens given parity of treatment and (b) non-EU citizens living abroad, and separately for the Curriculum in Arte and the Curriculum in Design within a single signed decree.
academic_requirements: Required qualification (one of): (a) a secondary school leaving certificate of the Italian system; or (b) an equivalent qualification obtained abroad. A foreign school-leaving certificate counts as equivalent only if obtained after 12 years of education AND the applicant attended at least the last two years in that foreign school system (unibz's own example: an Irish Leaving Certificate obtained after attending only one year is not enough). The Italian Ministry of Education, University and Research imposes additional specific requirements on holders of certain certificates — American high school diplomas, British and Greek certificates are named explicitly — and such applicants are told to contact apply@unibz.it (Advisory Service). Beyond the title, the applicant must fulfil the language requirements (B2 + B2), which are eliminatory. There is NO minimum school grade, NO subject prerequisite, NO mathematics requirement, no prior art-school requirement and no portfolio-of-prior-study requirement: unlike the engineering and economics bachelors, school marks play no part in the score — the 100 points come entirely from the video, the practical creative work and the interview. No ECTS/SSD credit requirements apply (bachelor level, so the 2024 SSD recoding such as INFO-01/A is irrelevant here). National rule: simultaneous enrolment in a maximum of 2 study programmes is permitted, provided the two do not belong to the same class (explicitly 'e.g., L-4/L-4') and differ in at least 2/3 of course contents — which rules out holding places on both the Art and the Design major of this same L-4 degree.
entry_exam_or_test: No written or standardised entrance examination of any kind. The list of instruments actually used is: (1) VIDEO, produced independently at home, uploaded to the application portal by the application deadline — max 2 minutes, max 150 MB, formats .mov/.mp4/.mpg/.avi/.wmv, file name surname_name.format; failure to upload by the deadline causes exclusion from the admission procedure. (2) PRACTICAL CREATIVE WORK, carried out entirely by the candidate at home; the topic and technical indications (size of models, materials, format, etc.) are e-mailed approximately one week before the interview, and the complete documentation must be sent by the modalities communicated with the topic — sending documentation by post is never allowed. (3) ONLINE INTERVIEW, about 10-15 minutes, before a commission of faculty lecturers. The only examinations connected with admission are the unibz Language Centre LANGUAGE exams, and only for candidates who choose that proof route: Early Bird — 16/03/2026 (registration 02-09/03/2026) and 16-17 and 20-21/04/2026 (registration 24/03-08/04/2026); Late — 22-26/06/2026 (registration 28/05-15/06/2026). NOTE: the Additional Application Session block publishes NO language exam dates, so that route appears unavailable for applicants in the currently open window. Only B2-level exams can be registered for. After admission there is also a non-selective third-language placement test for students who could not certify their third language.
selection_scoring: Maximum 100 points, awarded by a commission composed of lecturers of the faculty: VIDEO max 20 points (criteria: spirit of observation; judgement skill; creativity and originality); CREATIVE PRACTICAL WORK max 40 points, split into an evaluation for the DESIGN field max 20 points (spirit of observation; judgement skill; creativity and originality; design aspects in relation to implementation in the design field) and an evaluation in the field of ART max 20 points (spirit of observation; judgement skill; creativity and originality; artistic aspects in relation to implementation in the art field); INTERVIEW max 40 points (interdisciplinary interest; communication skill; creative skills). PUBLISHED THRESHOLDS: minimum 42/100 overall for admission to the Bachelor, PLUS a sub-threshold of minimum 8/20 in the ART-field evaluation of the practical creative work to be admitted to the Major in Art (symmetrically 8/20 in the Design field for the Major in Design). Tie-break order on equal total points: (1) interview score, (2) creative-practical-work score, (3) video score; only if those are also equal, the youngest candidate is chosen. ACTUAL 2026/27 RESULTS FOR THE MAJOR IN ART — far less competitive than the sibling Design major: Early Bird — only 7 admitted against 18 places, scores 94, 81, 73, 70, 63, 60, 58; NO waiting list; 4 candidates excluded on score (48 — this one having failed the 8/20 Art-field sub-threshold despite clearing 42 overall; 37; 15; and 4 for not submitting the creative work); 8 excluded for not possessing the admission requirements. Late — exactly 10 admitted against 10 places, scores 92, 89, 87, 83, 80, 70, 70, 66, 64, 63; NO waiting list; NO score-based exclusions at all; 6 excluded for not possessing the admission requirements. So in both sessions the effective cut-off equalled the published floor rather than exceeding it: every language-eligible candidate who cleared 42/100 and the 8/20 Art sub-threshold was admitted. Contrast with the Major in Design, where the effective cut-off was 57/100 in Early Bird and 47/100 in the Late session. The Art major's binding constraint is the language gate and the 8/20 Art-field sub-threshold, not the ranking.
bonus_points: None. The 100-point scale is exhausted by the three selection stages (20 + 40 + 40) and no bonus mechanism exists for this programme: there is NO Webometrics university-ranking bonus (that applies to the Master in Software Engineering and Master in Computing for Data Science), NO GMAT/GRE bonus (Accounting and Finance), NO startup-project bonus (Entrepreneurship and Innovation), no extracurricular-activity point (used by the Bachelor in Computer Science) and no bonus for school grades, prior art schooling, exhibitions, competitions or certificates. The CV is discussed in the interview but is not separately scored.
portfolio_and_materials: No conventional portfolio is requested — unibz replaces it with a video plus a commissioned home assignment. VIDEO: created independently at home, free choice of content; the brief specific to the Major in Art is 'Show us how you see the world around you. With a video in which you show your personality, your interest in art and your artistic goals, you demonstrate that you have the skills to become an art student. Be brave, surprise us!' — note this is worded differently from the Design brief, which asks the candidate to confront a two- or three-dimensional artefact and show a passion for design. Technical limits: length max 2 minutes; file size max 150 MB; accepted formats .mov, .mp4, .mpg, .avi, .wmv; file name must be surname_name.format. unibz explicitly reassures that professional equipment is not needed and the video 'does not have to be a perfect "Hollywood production". It's much more about good ideas!'. Applicants to BOTH majors must upload TWO different videos, one per major. The upload is a prerequisite: missing the deadline means exclusion from the admission procedure. PRACTICAL CREATIVE WORK: topic and technical indications (size of models, materials, format, etc.) are sent by e-mail approximately one week before the interview; it must be carried out entirely by the candidate; complete documentation must be submitted by the modalities communicated with the topic, and 'It is not allowed, in any case, to send the documentation of the work by post.' It must show spirit of observation, judgement and creativity. Non-submission is materially costly and is flagged on the ranking lists with a double asterisk — in the 2026/27 Art Early Bird list one candidate scored 4/100 for this reason. No motivation letter, no project proposal, no reference letters, no CV upload and no study-career Excel template are required. No page or character limits are published because no written dossier is requested.
interview: Yes — a compulsory online interview is the third and joint-heaviest stage (max 40 of 100 points). Conducted by a commission composed of lecturers of the faculty; duration about 10-15 minutes; the candidate receives an e-mail beforehand with all necessary information (time, platform to connect to). Content: show and explain the practical creative work to the commission; answer questions concerning the CV; answer general questions about design and/or art. Assessed on interdisciplinary interest, communication skill and creative skills. PUBLISHED 2026/27 DATES (Major in Art): Early Bird interview 15/05/2026; Late interview 17/07/2026; ADDITIONAL APPLICATION SESSION interview 16/09/2026 — this third date exists for the Major in Art only and not for the Major in Design. The interview score is also the first tie-break criterion on equal total points.
conditional_admission: There is no ECTS-threshold conditional-admission regime here — the ≥120/140 ECTS rule in the field schema is a MASTER-level provision and does not apply to this bachelor. The equivalent mechanisms are: (1) applicants still in their final school year apply normally and, if they gained (or will gain) their qualification abroad, upload the diploma at enrolment rather than at application — 'if you are not yet in possession of the diploma, you'll need to upload it upon enrolment'; (2) holders of a foreign qualification are subject to unibz's check of the foreign title, with the right to request additional documents in case of doubt, and exclusion by Rector's decree is possible even AFTER enrolment if the admission qualification turns out to be invalid; (3) the refund rule tied to this: fees paid to secure a place are not refundable unless the applicant fails the secondary-school final exam, or — for non-EU applicants living abroad — does not obtain the documents needed for enrolment from the Italian authorities in their country. [uncertain] — no separate late-enrolment window (such as the 11/12/2026 date used by some master programmes) is published for this programme; the last enrolment deadline for 2026/27 is 25/09/2026 noon, at the close of the Additional Application Session.
ofa_rules: OFA (Additional Learning Obligations / obblighi formativi aggiuntivi) applies here in a form unique among unibz bachelors — it is NOT tied to a mathematics test. The published rule: 'The Additional Learning Obligations are assigned if any weakness is found in your basic education.' Two concrete triggers: (1) LANGUAGE — 'You must fulfill Additional Learning Obligations in the third language if you have not certified level B1 in the third language'; (2) SELECTION SCORE — 'if you have been admitted to the BA and have achieved a score of less than 48 points in the selection procedure, you will receive Additional Learning Obligations.' The content of the OFA is defined before the start of the academic year by the Bachelor Study Council and published in the syllabi of the WUP Design and WUP Art projects (i.e. inside the Warm-Up project). The OFA is discharged by passing an exam. Practical effect in 2026/27 for the Major in Art: the score trigger bit hard, because the Art cut-offs sat near the floor. In the Early Bird session the last two admitted scored 60 and 58, so nobody was caught; but in the Late session FOUR of the ten admitted scored below 48 — ranks 8, 9 and 10 at 66, 64 and 63 are clear, yet the published Late scores are 92, 89, 87, 83, 80, 70, 70, 66, 64, 63, all above 48, so in fact no Late admittee was caught either. Where the 48-point line does matter for this major is that it sits only 6 points above the 42/100 admission floor, so any future admittee scraping in between 42 and 47 carries OFA automatically. Unlike the Computer Science ranking lists, the Design and Art lists do not mark OFA with an asterisk — the asterisks there flag the 8/20 Art-field sub-threshold failure (*) and non-submission of the creative work (**).
language_requirements: The official teaching languages are German, Italian and English, and the requirement is ELIMINATORY: 'The official teaching languages are German, Italian and English. Therefore, the following language requirements apply, otherwise you will be excluded from the admission procedure.' Entry: B2 in the 1st language AND B2 in the 2nd language; no level required in the 3rd. Exit (to graduate): C1 / C1 / B2, CEFR. Positions are defined by the candidate's own proficiency, not by the language: 'Your first language is the language in which you have the highest level of proficiency (B2 or C1). Your third language is instead the language in which you are weaker (or in which you are an absolute beginner).' Certification is MANDATORY for the 1st and 2nd language and recommended (from B1 upwards) for the 3rd, submitted in the application portal under 'upload language certificates' and/or 'enrol for language exams' after creating an application in 'create/manage applications'. A certificate awarded by an Italian public institution is submitted as a self-declaration; one awarded by a foreign public institution requires an uploaded scanned copy of the original. Programme-specific softening: 'A B1 level in the third language is the minimum requirement for taking curricular examinations in that specific language. In the first year of study, it is possible to sit exams relating to project-based activities before having achieved a B1 level in the third language' — i.e. the 19-CP studio projects and practical courses (drawing, studio, typography) are exempt from the B1 gate during year 1, while theoretical courses are not; from year 2 onwards B1 in the language of the course is required for all exams. Admitted students who cannot certify the third language sit a placement test (details by e-mail) and are assigned a learning path towards B2. Absolute beginners or anyone below B2 may attend a three-week intensive course in the September pre-semester session; A1 beginner courses are offered EXCLUSIVELY in that September session and no longer during the academic year, so absolute beginners must start there. During semesters there are extensive courses (4 h/week), between semesters intensive courses (6 h/day). All Language Centre courses are free of charge and target B1 in the third language by the end of year 1 and B2 by the end of year 2.
entry_levels_by_position: 1st language: B2 — 2nd language: B2 — 3rd language: no level required. This is the 'B2/B2/none' pattern shared with the trilingual engineering bachelors and with the sibling Major in Design, one step below the 'C1/B2/none' pattern of programmes such as Public Policy and Innovative Governance or Accounting and Finance. Position is determined by the candidate's own strength ranking and not by which language it is, so English B2 + Italian B2, English B2 + German B2 or Italian B2 + German B2 all satisfy the rule. Only B2-level exams can be registered for at the unibz Language Centre (the admission document repeats this sentence twice, verbatim and consecutively). B1 in the third language is not an admission condition but becomes the gate for sitting curricular exams in that language — with the year-1 exemption for project-based and practical activities described above. Practical note for the Art major specifically: because at least 25 CP of compulsory coursework is delivered only in German or Italian, choosing English as the 1st language and German as the 2nd is materially more useful here than English + Italian.
exit_levels: To graduate: 1st language C1, 2nd language C1, 3rd language B2 (CEFR). This is the standard unibz trilingual exit profile and is a genuine graduation gate: a student admitted at B2/B2/none must raise two languages to C1 and reach B2 in the third within the three years. Free Language Centre courses are structured to support this, targeting B1 in the third language by the end of year 1 and B2 by the end of year 2. For the Major in Art the exit requirement is especially consequential because three compulsory courses (Artistic Drawing 2D 8 CP, Drawing and Storytelling 6 CP, History of Contemporary Art 2 5 CP) are German-only, a compulsory choice group offers only German or Italian options, and two of the four studios ran without an English group in 2026/27.
third_language_exam_threshold: B1 in the third language is the minimum requirement for taking curricular examinations held in that language. Programme-specific relaxation, shared with the Major in Design: 'In the first year of study, it is possible to sit exams relating to project-based activities before having achieved a B1 level in the third language.' The Study Guide phrases the same rule from the course side — in year 1, theoretical courses require a certified B1 level in the language in which the course is offered, while practical courses (drawing, studio, typography) may be taken without it; from year 2 onwards, students must have certified B1 in the language of the course for all exams. If B1 in the third language is not certified, Additional Learning Obligations in the third language are assigned. There is NO mid-January English-B1 deadline of the kind imposed on the Bachelor in Computer Science, because the first semester here is not English-only.
proof_pathways: Four recognised pathways, plus a fifth route for bi-/multilingual and foreign schools. (1) The main teaching language of the final high school year, if German, Italian or English — recognised as C1; Ladin upper secondary schools are recognised as B2 in German and Italian; for foreign qualifications, if the main teaching language is not clearly stated on the diploma, a letter/document issued by the high school stating the medium of instruction must also be uploaded. (2) A bachelor or master degree in Italian, German or English — recognised as C1; unibz graduates upload the certificates obtained and/or declare Language Centre exams passed (B2, B2+ or C1); foreign degrees need a university letter stating the medium of instruction if it is not stated on the degree. (3) A recognised language certificate from the official unibz list; if it cannot be uploaded it may be sent by e-mail as a PDF or delivered in person to the Language Centre by the application deadline. (4) Language exams organised by the unibz Language Centre, registered online in the application portal under 'enrol for language exams' after filling out an application; if the application is started outside a registration period the candidate must return to the portal during one of the published periods. 2026/27 dates for this programme — Early Bird: exams 16/03/2026 (registration 02-09/03/2026) and 16-17 and 20-21/04/2026 (registration 24/03-08/04/2026); Late: exams 22-26/06/2026 (registration 28/05-15/06/2026). CRITICAL: the ADDITIONAL APPLICATION SESSION block lists no language exam dates at all, so pathway (4) appears closed for the currently open window and an applicant must rely on pathways (1), (2), (3) or (5) [uncertain — this is inferred from the absence of a 'Language exams' line in that block of the admission document, not from an explicit statement that the route is unavailable; confirm with apply@unibz.it]. Only B2-level exams can be registered for. (5) Secondary schools in a foreign country / bi- or multilingual schools: if CEFR levels for German, Italian or English (B1, B2 or C1) are explicitly indicated on the graduation diploma AND all four abilities (reading, listening, speaking, writing) were assessed, the indicated levels are accepted as proof for the 2nd and/or 3rd language; the school-leaving certificate must be uploaded under the respective language and the Language Centre decides on recognition.
certificate_rules: Governed by Resolution of the University Council n. 16/2026 ('Recognised language certificates and diplomas - Students and applicants'). To be recognised a certificate must: (1) include assessment of all FOUR skills and be issued by the certification provider itself; (2) show a sufficient result in each skill as an overall grade, or have the detailed assessment stated on the certificate or in appropriate documentation from the provider. If no overall result and/or level is stated, THE LOWEST LEVEL REACHED IN ANY SUB-SKILL determines the recognised level, provided that part was passed. There is no compensation for failed parts of the exam and no averages are calculated unless the certification provider itself does so. Certificates obtained through remote 'home edition' exams are NOT recognised, except those explicitly flagged in the list. Certificates covering single skills issued by different organisations are not accepted. Certificates of participation, end-of-course tests and exams from private educational institutions, and placement-test results are not recognised. Certificates issued by individual lecturers, lectors or teachers are not recognised, and DAAD certificates are expressly NOT recognised. Validity: international language certificates must have been obtained within the five years preceding submission, counting whole calendar years from 1 January (certificates issued from 1 January of the fifth preceding year, valid for that whole year). Items listed under 'Further Recognised Degrees, Diplomas and Certificates' have unlimited validity. Full list: https://www.unibz.it/assets/Documents/Languages/unibz-recognised-language-certificates-v2.pdf
application_deadline_eu: THREE sessions for EU citizens and citizens given parity of treatment in 2026/27 — one more than the Major in Design (unibz publishes DD/MM/YYYY; ISO given below). (1) Early Bird Application: 02/03/2026 - 28/04/2026 by noon local time = 2026-03-02 to 2026-04-28, with the video upload due by the same deadline, 28/04/2026 noon. (2) Late Application (EU citizens only): 28/05/2026 - 02/07/2026 by noon local time = 2026-05-28 to 2026-07-02, video upload by 02/07/2026 noon. NOTE the Late window closes SIX DAYS EARLIER than the engineering/economics bachelors' 08/07/2026 — it is programme-specific. (3) ADDITIONAL APPLICATION SESSION (EU citizens only): 18/08/2026 - 04/09/2026 by noon local time = 2026-08-18 to 2026-09-04, video upload by 04/09/2026 noon. This third window exists because both regular sessions underfilled (17 admitted against 28 EU places) and, as of the verification date 2026-08-29, it is OPEN with six days remaining — the Major in Art is one of only two Faculty of Design and Art programmes in the additional session (the other being the Master in Critical Creative Practices), and the sibling Major in Design is NOT in it. EU applicants may apply for more than one study programme, and an applicant excluded in the first session may apply again in the second (in 2026/27 at least two candidates excluded or heavily penalised in Early Bird were admitted in the Late session).
application_deadline_non_eu: ONE window only for non-EU citizens living outside Italy: the Early Bird Application, 02/03/2026 - 28/04/2026 by noon local time = 2026-03-02 to 2026-04-28, with the video uploaded to the application portal by 28/04/2026 noon, the online interview on 15/05/2026 and the ranking list by 27/05/2026. 'Only one application period is offered. After the deadline it is not possible to apply anymore.' Non-EU applicants living abroad are NOT eligible for the Late Application and NOT eligible for the Additional Application Session (both are explicitly labelled 'only for EU citizens'), pay a non-refundable €50 application fee, are ranked on a separate list against a separate 2-place quota, and must additionally pre-enrol on the Universitaly portal (one programme only) to obtain the study visa. In 2026/27 the Early Bird ranking decree contained NO non-EU section for the Curriculum in Arte at all — not even an exclusion list — so both non-EU places went unused, and for a non-EU applicant living abroad the 2026/27 cycle is now definitively closed; the next opportunity is the 2027/28 Early Bird window, expected around March-April 2027.
parity_of_treatment: Two categories are treated as EU applicants — the critical third category for Turkish and other non-EU nationals: (1) citizens of Norway, Iceland, Liechtenstein, Switzerland, San Marino and the Vatican City State; (2) non-EU citizens holding a valid Italian permit to stay ('permesso di soggiorno') under article 39 paragraph 5 of decree no. 286 of 25.07.1998 — for WORK, FAMILY reasons, POLITICAL or HUMANITARIAN ASYLUM, or RELIGIOUS reasons. These applicants apply directly to the University and must submit a copy of the valid permit to stay; if the permit has expired a renewal request must be attached. A permit to stay for STUDY reasons or a visa for tourism is NOT sufficient. Critical warning reproduced in the admission document: if the permit is not uploaded in the application portal, the applicant 'will be automatically considered a non-EU citizen living abroad and therefore subject to the admission procedure through the Italian authorities in your country of origin'. For the Major in Art specifically the cost of that mistake is unusually high: it means losing access to the Late session AND to the Additional Application Session (both EU-only), and competing instead for just 2 places in a single spring window — a window in which, in 2026/27, not a single non-EU applicant made it onto the list.
places_quotas: Two separate quotas for the Major in Art in 2026/27. EU citizens and citizens given parity of treatment: Early Bird Application 18 places, Late Application 10 places (28 EU in total — the programme page and brochure summarise this as 'Places available: 28 EU + 2 non-EU'). Non-EU citizens living abroad: Early Bird Application 2 places, and no non-EU quota in any later session. Carry-over rule: for EU citizens and citizens given parity of treatment only, any places remaining unfilled after the Early Bird session are offered in the Late Application. Actual 2026/27 uptake — the Art major UNDERFILLED: Early Bird admitted only 7 of 18 places with no waiting list; the Late session admitted exactly 10 (its own quota) with no waiting list, despite the 11 unfilled Early Bird places having carried over; and both non-EU places went unfilled with no non-EU applicants listed at all. Total admitted 17 against 28 EU + 2 non-EU = 30 places, leaving roughly 11 EU places, which is why the Faculty opened the Additional Application Session for 18/08-04/09/2026. [uncertain] — no explicit number of places is published for the Additional Application Session either in the admission document or on the additional-session page; the ~11 figure is arithmetic from the published quotas minus the published admitted counts and may differ from the number the Faculty actually releases. Contrast with the sibling Major in Design: 34 EU Early Bird + 24 EU Late + 2 non-EU, both EU quotas filled exactly with real waiting lists, and therefore no additional session.
ranking_and_enrolment_dates: Early Bird (Major in Art): interview 15/05/2026; ranking lists published by 27/05/2026 (the actual decree carries protocol no. 0015024/26 dated 18/05/2026); payment of the 1st instalment of the tuition fees (€600, the payment that secures the place) by 05/06/2026 noon local time; enrolment from 10/07/2026 to 06/08/2026 noon. NOTE: because only 7 candidates were admitted and no waiting list was drawn up for the Art major, the 08/06/2026 waiting-list call-up date printed in the decree applies to the Design major only. Late Application: interview 17/07/2026; ranking lists published by 23/07/2026 (decree protocol no. 0021217/26 dated 21/07/2026 — one week earlier than the 30/07/2026 used by other faculties); 1st instalment by 06/08/2026 noon; enrolment from publication of the ranking list until 06/08/2026 noon; again no waiting list for the Art major. ADDITIONAL APPLICATION SESSION: interview 16/09/2026; ranking lists published by 18/09/2026 (not yet published as of 2026-08-29); 1st instalment by 25/09/2026 noon; enrolment from publication of the ranking list until 25/09/2026 noon — a very compressed 7-day window between ranking and enrolment close. Missing either the payment or the enrolment deadline means automatic exclusion and the place passes to the next applicant on the ranking list. A candidate admitted to more than one programme may secure up to 2 places by paying the designated rate twice. Paying the fees does NOT confer student status — only enrolment does — and there is no refund if you pay but do not enrol (exceptions: failing the secondary-school final exam, or, for non-EU applicants abroad, not obtaining the necessary documents from the Italian authorities in their country). Enrolment as early as possible is recommended so that incomplete documents can still be uploaded before the deadline. Ranking lists are valid only for the respective academic year.
programme_specific_dates: Programme-specific admission dates for 2026/27 (Major in Art): video upload deadlines 28/04/2026 noon (Early Bird), 02/07/2026 noon (Late) and 04/09/2026 noon (Additional Session) — identical to the respective application deadlines and an absolute prerequisite; ONLINE INTERVIEWS 15/05/2026, 17/07/2026 and 16/09/2026 (the third date is unique to the Art major); the topic and technical indications of the practical creative work are e-mailed approximately ONE WEEK BEFORE each interview, i.e. around 08/05/2026, around 10/07/2026 and around 09/09/2026 [uncertain — 'approximately one week before' is the published wording; unibz does not publish the exact send dates]; Language Centre exams 16/03/2026 (registration 02-09/03/2026), 16-17 and 20-21/04/2026 (registration 24/03-08/04/2026) and 22-26/06/2026 (registration 28/05-15/06/2026), with NO exam session published for the Additional Session. The programme has NO pre-course period of the kind published for the engineering bachelors. Compulsory safety training (Work Safety - Machinery Hazard - Chemical Risk) must be completed before workshop courses; the Warm-Up introductory workshop courses in semester 1 are compulsory to access the specialised workshops.
required_documents: At application, online via the Application Portal (https://aws.unibz.it/exup): create an account and upload a valid ID card or passport, front and back — 'if your document is invalid, incomplete or unreadable, you will be excluded from the admission procedure'; fill in the online form and upload the attachments listed under 'Admission procedure'; upload the VIDEO (max 2 min, max 150 MB, .mov/.mp4/.mpg/.avi/.wmv, named surname_name.format) by the application deadline — two separate videos if applying to both majors; upload language certificates under 'upload language certificates' (mandatory for the 1st and 2nd language, recommended for the 3rd from B1 upwards) and/or register for Language Centre exams under 'enrol for language exams'; a self-declaration if the final language certificate was awarded by an Italian public institution, or a scanned copy of the original if awarded by a foreign public institution; if the qualification was gained abroad, the diploma of the qualification (if not yet held, it is uploaded at enrolment); for non-EU citizens resident in Italy claiming parity of treatment, a copy of the valid permit to stay (plus a renewal request if expired). Then, after the deadline, the documentation of the PRACTICAL CREATIVE WORK, submitted by the modalities communicated by e-mail together with the topic — never by post. NOTE: there is no motivation letter, no CV upload, no reference letters and NO study-career Excel template (that structured upload is a master-level requirement). Once the application has been sent it cannot be modified, and 'Filled-in forms which have not been sent correctly will not be taken into consideration.' Mendacious declarations are criminally prosecuted and result in automatic exclusion from the ranking list. At enrolment, holders of a foreign secondary school qualification must additionally upload the secondary school diploma, an official translation into Italian (not necessary for diplomas issued in German or English), and the ARDI/CIMEA statements described under credential_recognition. Students transferring from another Italian university must submit a copy of the transfer application to the Student Office at the beginning of the academic year. Non-EU students must hand in the residence permit to the Student Office personally or by e-mail once obtained.
application_fee: €50, payable only by non-EU citizens living outside Italy. It is described as an administration fee and is explicitly non-refundable. EU citizens and citizens given parity of treatment — including non-EU nationals holding a qualifying Italian permit to stay for work, family, asylum or religious reasons — pay no application fee, and this exemption extends to the Late and Additional Application Sessions, which only they may enter.
tuition_or_fees_link: Tuition fees amount to €1,200 per year in two instalments: 1st instalment €600, which includes the €16 revenue stamp (marca da bollo) and is the payment that secures the place after admission; 2nd instalment €600, to be paid by March of the following year. Delayed payment of the second instalment incurs a fine; unpaid fees block exam-taking and any transfer to another university or study programme. No reimbursement if you drop out, interrupt your studies or are excluded. Exemptions: students with a disability recognised under article 3 paragraph 1 of Law No 104/1992 or with a disability up to or exceeding 66% (health-authority certificate to be handed in at the beginning of the academic year), and foreign students who have been granted a scholarship from the Italian government. Students who benefit from a scholarship granted by the Autonomous Province of Bozen-Bolzano are entitled to a refund of the tuition fees. Not included in the €1,200: materials, models, photographic/video production and workshop consumables, which for a studio-based art degree with sculpture, installation, photography and film work are a real additional cost [uncertain — unibz publishes no estimate of material costs for this programme]. Fees pages: https://guide.unibz.it/en/study-career/general-information/fees/ and the programme's admission-information PDF at https://www.unibz.it/assets/CoursesPDF/bachelor-in-design-and-art-major-in-art_admission-information_en_GB.pdf
scholarships_grants: The main route is the income-based study grant of the Autonomous Province of South Tyrol / Bozen-Bolzano, awarded through its Office for the Right to Study; the Province offers three instruments — ordinary study grants, merit scholarships and postgraduate study grants — applied for online through the provincial e-government service, with help available from the South Tyrolean Students Association. Grant holders also receive a refund of the tuition fees paid. Other funding sources named by unibz are the Italian government, the Austrian and German governments and private banks. CRITICAL RESTRICTION FOR INTERNATIONAL STUDENTS: non-EU students can apply for a study grant only if they have a long-term residence permit or after they have had their residence in South Tyrol for at least one year without interruption — so a newly arrived non-EU first-year student is effectively ineligible in year one. unibz itself grants tuition-fee exemptions rather than cash scholarships at bachelor level (disability, Italian government scholarship holders). No programme-specific scholarship is published for the Bachelor in Design and Art - Major in Art. [uncertain] — the frequently cited grant range of roughly €1,680-€6,960 per year, the merit threshold (e.g. a 27/30 average after the first year) and the annual application deadlines are NOT stated on the pages verified for this programme; amounts and deadlines are set annually by the provincial call and must be checked there. Reference page: https://guide.unibz.it/en/life-on-campus/study-grants
credential_recognition: At enrolment, holders of a foreign secondary school qualification must upload the diploma plus an official translation into Italian (not necessary for diplomas issued in German or English), and then, depending on the education system: (a) EU countries, Switzerland, Norway, Iceland, Liechtenstein, International Baccalaureate, European Baccalaureate — a Statement of Correspondence of the secondary school diploma, to be downloaded from ARDI, the Automatic Recognition Database - Italy (https://ardi.cimea.it/en); (b) non-EU countries that ARE signatories to the Lisbon Convention — a Statement of Correspondence from ARDI AND a Statement of Verification of the secondary school diploma issued by CIMEA, the Italian Information Centre on Academic Mobility and Equivalence; (c) non-EU countries that are NOT signatories of the Lisbon Convention — a Statement of Comparability issued by CIMEA AND a Statement of Verification issued by CIMEA. Türkiye is a signatory of the Lisbon Recognition Convention, so Turkish applicants normally fall under case (b): ARDI Statement of Correspondence + CIMEA Statement of Verification. unibz performs the necessary checks on the foreign qualification and reserves the right to request additional documents in case of doubt; an applicant found not to possess a valid admission qualification can be excluded by Rector's decree even after enrolment. Signatory list: https://www.enic-naric.net/ ; CIMEA services: https://cimea-diplome.it/ . Separately, recognition of credit points from previous university studies is possible only after enrolment and only where the exams taken at the university of provenance are equivalent in content to those offered at unibz.
non_eu_visa_process: Sequence for non-EU citizens living abroad: apply to unibz in the Early Bird window only, 02/03-28/04/2026, paying the €50 non-refundable fee → upload the video and complete the three-stage selection (interview 15/05/2026) → appear on the separate non-EU ranking list (2 places) → if admitted, secure the place by paying the €600 first instalment by 05/06/2026 noon → THEN start the visa application on the Universitaly portal of the Ministry of University and Research. The Universitaly application is MANDATORY, 'otherwise you will not be allowed to enrol', and only ONE study programme may be selected there. The Italian diplomatic-consular representation in the applicant's country then issues the entry visa for studies/university, which allows enrolment in the programme applied for. unibz warns that admission to unibz confers no automatic right to a visa, which is the exclusive responsibility of embassies and consulates. Financial means for the visa: at least €800 per month for living costs in the Bozen-Bolzano area excluding tuition fees, with a bachelor programme costed at a minimum of €36,000 overall (€24,000 for a master). Health insurance is required. After arrival: under Italian law the residence permit ('permesso di soggiorno') must be APPLIED FOR within 8 working days of arrival in Italy — contact the Advisory Service immediately on arrival — and once obtained a copy must be handed in at the Student Office personally or via e-mail. Student work is limited to no more than 20 hours a week and no more than 1,040 hours per year. Refund exception: non-EU applicants abroad who pay the instalment but do not obtain the necessary documents for enrolment from the Italian authorities in their country are entitled to a refund. IMPORTANT for this programme: the Late and Additional Application Sessions are explicitly EU-only, so a non-EU applicant living abroad has exactly one attempt per year, and the 2026/27 attempt has passed. What is solid is that this major has no all-English semester, that at least 25 CP of compulsory credit cannot be taken in English, and that in 2026/27 two of the four studios ran with no English group. (7) The claim that an English-reliant student cannot assemble four studio instances from English groups alone follows from the 2026/27 tags combined with the rule that Studio A and Studio D can each be taken only once — it is an inference from two published sources, not a unibz statement.
